NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using top-oil temperature as the primary indicator with fixed thresholds. My same-class departure is a dynamic thermal model integrating load current and ambient temperature to compute the *equivalent hotspot temperature* as the primary indicator, capturing transient aging effects missed by static thresholds. The failure-physics connection is Arrhenius aging: hotspot temperature drives insulation degradation exponentially, and load current modulates hotspot temperature via winding resistance (I²R heating) and oil convection.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Equivalent Hotspot Temperature (θ_h) = Top-Oil Temperature (θ_o) + Δθ_h, where Δθ_h = K · I² · R · (θ_o - θ_a) / (θ_o + 273) (K = transformer-specific constant from nameplate). Magnitude verification: For 40 MVA ONAN, Δθ_h ≈ 10–15°C at full load (stated spec), making θ_h 10–15°C higher than θ_o—sufficient to detect aging precursors (Arrhenius sensitivity: 2× life change per 6°C).  

DIRECTION OF EFFECT: driving variable = equivalent hotspot temperature (θ_h); the mechanism moves it DOWN by modulating load current via duty-cycle adjustments; this LOWERS the Arrhenius aging integral (exp(-Ea/θ_h)).  

INPUT INVENTORY:  
- Top-oil temperature (θ_o) — source: ALREADY-RECORDED("top-oil temperature")  
- Load current (I) — source: ALREADY-RECORDED("load current")  
- Ambient temperature (θ_a) — source: ALREADY-RECORDDED("ambient temperature")  
- Transformer resistance (R) — source: DERIVED(stated nameplate resistance at 75°C)  
- Constant K — source: DERIVED(stated hot-spot gradient from factory test reports)  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
MECHANISM CLASS: dynamic thermal load modulation  
(a) Data acquisition module: Existing SCADA system (ALREADY-RECORDED) for θ_o, I, θ_a.  
(b) Thermal model processor: Embedded algorithm computing θ_h = θ_o + K·I²·R·(θ_o - θ_a)/(θ_o + 273).  
(c) Aging-rate calculator: Arrhenius model: aging rate = A·exp(-B/θ_h) (A, B from stated insulation class).  
(d) Remaining-life predictor: Integrate aging rate over time; trigger alert when remaining life ≤ 30 days.  
(e) Load-shedding scheduler: Duty-cycle controller reducing I by 5–10% when θ_h > threshold (CALCULATED: θ_h_threshold = θ_o_nominal + 10°C, from stated hotspot margin).  
(f) Alert interface: Existing transformer protection relay (ALREADY-RECORDED) for trip-warning signals.  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as standard (no new hardware; software-only).  
- Operability: Minimal training (uses existing SCADA).  
- Maintenance: Zero (no moving parts; constants from nameplate).  
- Cost class: Same (software-only vs. static relay upgrades).  
- Operational cost: Throughput reduction ≤5% during alerts (UNPRICED_OPERATIONAL_LOSS: 5% energy loss, justified by avoiding 1 FA/year).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Simulate 30-day aging precursor by ramping I to 110% rated while θ_a = 40°C (stated max).  
Instruments: Existing SCADA logs (ALREADY-RECORDED), oscilloscope for I/θ_o.  
Pass/fail: Alert within 24 hours of θ_h exceeding threshold; no false trip during normal operation.  
Duration: 72-hour simulation.  
Kill criterion: Failure to alert or false trip.  
Validation: Against stated thermal time constant (CALCULATED: 2–4 hours for ONAN).  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Equivalent hotspot temperature (θ_h), as it directly governs Arrhenius aging. Top-oil temperature is secondary (supplements but does not replace θ_h).  

DIRECTION-CORRECTNESS CLAUSE  
The driving quantity is θ_h; the mechanism reduces it by lowering I (down) via duty-cycle modulation, which reduces I²R heating and thus θ_h, lowering the Arrhenius integral (exp(-Ea/θ_h)).  

INPUT-AVAILABILITY CLAUSE  
All signals (θ_o, I, θ_a) are ALREADY-RECORDED per problem constraints; no new instrumentation.  

COST-PRICING CLAUSE  
Operational cost: 5% energy throughput reduction during alerts (order-of-magnitude bound: ≤2 MWh/year for 40 MVA). Trade nets positive: avoids 1 FA/year (cost > $500k).

MECHANISM CLASS: dynamic thermal load modulation (distinct from standard static monitoring).
